items.prompt:
The Sun gives off
A) light and warmth
B) only sound
C) only wind
D) rain

steps: The Sun gives off light and warmth.

items.prompt:
Sunlight on Earth's surface
A) warms it
B) cools it
C) does nothing
D) makes it dark

steps: Sunlight warms the surfaces it shines on.

items.prompt:
Which feels warmer?
A) A bench in the sun
B) A bench in the shade
C) They are always the same
D) Neither is warm
items.answer: A) A bench in the sun

steps: The sunny bench is warmed by sunlight.

items.prompt:
Shady ground is usually ____ than sunny ground.
A) warmer
B) cooler
C) exactly the same
D) brighter

steps: Shade blocks sunlight, so it stays cooler.

items.prompt:
A puddle in the sun dries faster than one in the shade because sunlight
A) cools the water
B) warms the water and dries it faster
C) adds more water
D) does nothing
items.answer: B) warms the water and dries it faster

steps: The Sun's warmth speeds up drying.

items.prompt:
The longer the Sun shines on something, the
A) cooler it gets
B) warmer it gets
C) smaller it gets
D) darker it gets

steps: More sunlight over time warms it more.

items.prompt:
A rock in the sun all afternoon will feel ____ than it did in the morning shade.
A) cooler
B) warmer
C) the same
D) wetter

steps: Sunlight has been warming the rock all afternoon.

items.prompt:
The BEST way to observe that sunlight warms the ground is to
A) guess
B) compare how warm a sunny spot and a shady spot feel
C) look at the sky
D) close your eyes
items.answer: B) compare how warm a sunny spot and a shady spot feel

steps: Comparing sunny and shady spots shows the warming effect.
